verses.text: Theophilus, in my first book I wrote about all the things that Jesus did and what He told people to do while He was here on earth.
Before Jesus went to heaven, Jesus chose 12 men to be His apostles. Jesus and the Holy Spirit told them what to do when He had gone away.

After Jesus had suffered and died, He started to live again, and He came to the apostles and showed them that He was alive. He appeared to them a lot of times in 40 days, and He told them about God who is King over everyone.
And when they came together, Jesus gave them this order: Do not leave Jerusalem, but wait for the gift I told you about, the gift my Father promised.
John baptized with water, but in a few days, you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
The apostles were all together. They asked Jesus: Lord, is this the time for You to give the people of Israel their kingdom again?
Jesus said to them: The Father is the only one who has the authority to decide dates and times. They are not for you to know.
But when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, you will be filled with power, and you will be witnesses for me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
After Jesus said this, He was lifted up into the sky. While they were watching, He went into a cloud, and they could not see Him anymore.
They were staring into the sky where He had gone. Suddenly two men wearing white clothes were standing beside them.
They said: Men from Galilee, why are you standing here looking into the sky? You saw Jesus carried away from you into heaven. He will come back in the same way you saw Him go.

Then the apostles went back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives. This mountain is about a Sabbath day's journey from Jerusalem — roughly three-quarters of a mile, the distance a person was allowed to walk on the Sabbath under Jewish tradition.

They entered the city and went up to the room where they were staying: Peter, John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, Simon the Patriot, and Judas son of James.
The apostles always prayed together with a few women and with Mary, the mother of Jesus, and His brothers were also with them.
One day there were about 120 believers together and Peter got up and said to them:

Friends, long ago the Holy Spirit told King David to write about Judas in the Old Testament. That is what has happened now. Judas went to the Jewish leaders, and he told them how they could catch Jesus.
Judas was one of us and he worked with us,
but then he took the money that the Jewish leaders gave him, and he bought a field. A few days later he fell on his face. His stomach burst open, and his insides came out.
When they told the people of Jerusalem what had happened, they said the name of that field in their own language would be Akeldama. It means Field of blood.
We read these words in the book of Psalms: His house must be empty, and no one must live there. And: Someone else must do his work.

1.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. A merged-verse numbering bug (16/17) has been split apart, and a fragment sentence in v2 fixed.

verses.text: When the day of Pentecost came, all the believers were together in one place.
Suddenly a sound came from heaven, like a strong wind blowing hard, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
They saw what looked like small flames of fire. The flames separated, and one flame came down and rested on each person.
The Holy Spirit filled all of them. Then they began to speak in other languages, because the Spirit gave them the power to do this.
At that time, many faithful Jews were living in Jerusalem. They had come from every nation in the world.
When the people heard this sound, a crowd gathered. They were confused, because each person heard the message in their own language.
They were amazed and surprised. They asked: Are all these people who are speaking not from Galilee?
Then how can each of us hear them speaking in our own language?
We are Parthians, Medes, and Elamites. We are from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia.
We are from Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, and the parts of Libya near Cyrene. Others of us have come to visit from Rome.

Some of us are Jews by birth, and others became Jews later. Some of us are from Crete, and some are from Arabia. But all of us hear these men speaking in our own languages about the wonderful things God has done!
The people were amazed and confused. They asked each other: What does this mean?
But others mocked them and said: They have had too much wine.

Then Peter stood up with the eleven apostles. He raised his voice and spoke to the crowd: My Jewish brothers, and all of you who live in Jerusalem, let me explain this to you. Listen carefully to what I say.
These people are not drunk, like you think. It is only nine o'clock in the morning!
No, this is what the prophet Joel spoke about long ago:
In the last days, God says: I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your young people will see visions, and your elders will dream dreams.
Even on my servants, both men and women, I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.
I will show wonders in the heavens above and signs on the earth below — blood and fire and clouds of smoke.
The sun will turn dark, and the moon will turn red like blood. This will happen before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.
And everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved.

My fellow Israelites, listen to this: Jesus of Nazareth was a man that God showed to you. God proved this through the miracles and wonders and signs that God did through Jesus. You yourselves already know this.
God planned this before it happened, and God knew it would happen. Then wicked men helped hand Jesus over to you, and you nailed Him to a cross and killed Him.
But God raised Jesus back to life. God set Jesus free from the pain of death, because death could not hold on to Jesus.
David said about Jesus: I always saw the Lord in front of me. Because He is at my right hand, I will not be moved.
So my heart is glad and my words are full of joy. My body will rest, knowing that I can trust God's promise,
Because You will not leave me dead in the grave. You will not let Your holy one's body decay.
You have shown me the way that leads to life. You will fill me with joy when I am with You.
My fellow Israelites, I can tell you for certain that our ancestor David died and was buried. His tomb is still here today.
But David was a prophet. He knew that God had made a promise to him: God would put one of David's own family on David's throne.
David saw ahead of time what would happen, and he spoke about the Messiah rising from death. He said that the Messiah would not be left in the grave, and His body would not decay.
God has raised this Jesus to life, and we are all witnesses of it.
God lifted Jesus up to the highest place, at God's right hand. Jesus received the Holy Spirit that the Father had promised, and Jesus poured out the Spirit. That is what you now see and hear.
David did not go up into heaven himself, but David said: The LORD said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
Until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet.
So let all of Israel know for certain: God has made this Jesus, the same Jesus you nailed to the cross, both Lord and Messiah.
When the people heard this, they felt very sorry in their hearts. They said to Peter and the other apostles: Brothers, what should we do?
Peter answered: Each of you must turn away from your sins and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, so that your sins will be forgiven. Then you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
The promise is for you and your children and for all who are far off — for all whom the Lord our God will call.
Peter said many other words to warn them, and he begged them: Save yourselves from these evil, sinful people of today.
Those who believed Peter's message were baptized. That day about three thousand people joined the believers.
The believers kept on learning from the apostles' teaching. They spent time together, ate meals together, and prayed together.
Everyone felt amazed and full of wonder, and the apostles did many wonders and miracles.
All the believers stayed together, and they shared everything they had.
They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need.
Every day they kept meeting together at the temple. They ate meals together in their homes with glad and honest hearts,
They praised God, and all the people liked them. Every day the Lord added more people to the group, people who were being saved.

2.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Pentecost, the coming of the Holy Spirit and speaking in tongues, Peter's sermon (including his quotation of Psalm 16), and the birth of the early church. V27 and v31 render 'hell' as 'the grave,' since the underlying reference (through the Greek Hades, translating Hebrew Sheol in the psalm being quoted) is to the realm of the dead, not Gehenna -- matching this site's standing convention. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard. V38 deliberately renders the Greek preposition 'eis' as 'because of' rather than the more standard 'for,' reflecting the pastor's chosen position in the ongoing debate over what baptism accomplishes. This 'causal eis' reading has real grammatical support (notably A.T. Robertson, citing the parallel in Matthew 12:41 -- 'they repented at [eis] the preaching of Jonah,' i.e. in response to it) but remains a minority position; most modern grammars (e.g. Daniel Wallace) favor the purpose/result sense reflected in KJV, NIV, ESV, and NASB, partly because the identical phrase 'eis aphesin hamartion' in Mark 1:4 and Matthew 26:28 is not typically read causally.

verses.text: One day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the time of prayer — at three in the afternoon.

There was a man who could not walk since he was born. Every day, people carried him to the temple gate called Beautiful. They put him there so he could beg for money from the people going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John about to enter, he asked them for money.
Peter looked directly at him, as did John. Then Peter said: Look at us!
So the man looked closely at them. He hoped they would give him something.
Then Peter said: I do not have silver or gold, but I will give you what I have. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk!
Peter took the man by his right hand and helped him stand up. Right away, the man's feet and ankles became strong.
He jumped to his feet and began to walk. Then he went with them into the temple courts, walking, jumping, and praising God.
When all the people saw him walking and praising God,
They recognized him. He was the same man who used to sit and beg at the temple gate called Beautiful. The people were filled with wonder and amazement at what had happened to him.
While the man held on to Peter and John, all the people were amazed. They came running to them in the place called Solomon's Porch.
When Peter saw this, he spoke to the crowd: My fellow Israelites, why does this surprise you? Why do you stare at us like we made this man walk by our own power or our own goodness?

The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the God of our ancestors, has given honor and glory to His servant Jesus. You handed Jesus over to be killed, and you said you did not know Him in front of Pilate, even though Pilate had decided to let Jesus go free.
You said you did not know the Holy and Good One, and you asked for a murderer to be set free instead.
You killed the one who gives life, but God raised Him back to life. We are witnesses of this.

This man, the one you see and know, was made strong because of faith in the name of Jesus. It is His name, and the faith that comes through Jesus, that has completely healed him. You can all see this.
Now, brothers and sisters, I know that you did not understand what you were doing, and your leaders did not understand either.
But this is how God made happen what He had said long ago through all the prophets: that His Messiah would suffer.
So turn away from your sins and turn to God. Then your sins will be forgiven, and good times of new strength will come to you from the Lord,
And then God will send Jesus, the Messiah He has chosen for you.
Jesus must stay in heaven until the time comes for God to make everything right again. God promised this long ago through His holy prophets.
For Moses said: The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people. You must listen to everything He tells you.
Anyone who does not listen to Him will be completely removed from among their people.
In fact, all the prophets, starting with Samuel, spoke about these days that are happening now.
And the promises that the prophets gave belong to you. So does the promise God made with your ancestors. God said to Abraham: Through your family, all people on earth will be blessed.
When God raised up His servant, God sent Jesus to you first, to bless you by turning each of you away from your sinful ways.

3.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the healing of the man lame from birth at the temple's Beautiful Gate, and Peter's sermon to the astonished crowd in Solomon's Colonnade. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard, with Jesus and God renamed explicitly at intervals throughout Peter's sermon to avoid long unbroken runs of pronouns.

verses.text: While Peter and John were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple guard, and the Sadducees came up to them.
They were very upset because the apostles were teaching the people and preaching that people could rise from the dead through Jesus.
They grabbed Peter and John. Because it was already evening, they put them in jail until the next day.
But many who heard the message believed, and the number of men who believed grew to about five thousand.
The next day the rulers, elders, and teachers of the law met in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there, and so were Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and others of the high priest's family.
They brought Peter and John in front of them and began to question them: By what power, or in what name, did you do this?
Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: Rulers and elders of the people!
Today you are questioning us about a good deed we did for a man who could not walk. You are asking us how he was healed.

Then all of you, and all the people of Israel, must know this: This man stands before you healed because of the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth. You nailed Jesus to a cross and killed Him, but God raised Him from the dead.
Jesus is the stone you builders rejected, which has become the cornerstone.
No one else can save us. There is no other name under heaven given to people by which we must be saved.
The leaders saw how bold Peter and John were. They realized these were ordinary men with no special training. The leaders were amazed, and they recognized that these men had been with Jesus.
But the man who had been healed was standing right there with them, so the leaders could not say anything against it.
So they told Peter and John to leave the council room, and then the leaders talked among themselves.
They asked: What are we going to do with these men? Everyone living in Jerusalem knows they have done a clear miracle, and we cannot say it is not true.
But we must warn them to stop speaking to anyone in this name, so this does not spread any further among the people.
Then they called them in again and commanded them not to speak or teach at all in the name of Jesus.
But Peter and John replied: Which is right in God's eyes: to listen to you, or to listen to God? You be the judges!
As for us, we cannot help speaking about what we have seen and heard.
After further threats they let them go. They could not decide how to punish them, because all the people were praising God for what had happened.
The man who was healed by this miracle was over forty years old.
On their release, Peter and John went back to their own people and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.
When they heard this, they all prayed together out loud to God: Lord and Master, You made the heavens, the earth, the sea, and everything in them.
Long ago, You spoke through the Holy Spirit, using the words of Your servant, our father David: Why are the nations so angry? Why do the people make useless plans?
The kings of the earth stand up to fight, and the rulers join together against the Lord and against His Anointed One.
This is exactly what happened: Herod and Pontius Pilate met together with the non-Jewish people and the people of Israel in this city to plan against Your holy servant Jesus, the one You anointed.
They did only what Your power and Your plan had already decided would happen.
Now, Lord, look at how they are threatening us. Help Your servants to speak Your word with great boldness.
Stretch out Your hand to heal, and perform signs and wonders through the name of Your holy servant Jesus.
After they prayed, the place where they were meeting was shaken. And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God boldly.
All the believers were one in heart and mind. No one claimed that any of their possessions was their own, but they shared everything they had.
With great power the apostles kept telling everyone that the Lord Jesus had risen from the dead. God's grace was working powerfully in all of them,
So there was no one among them who was in need. From time to time, people who owned land or houses would sell them and bring the money from the sale.
And put it at the apostles' feet, and it was distributed to anyone who had need.
Joseph, a Levite from Cyprus, whom the apostles called Barnabas (which means son of encouragement),
Sold a field he owned and brought the money and put it at the apostles' feet.

4.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Peter and John's arrest, their defense before the Sanhedrin (including the famous 'no other name' declaration and 'we cannot help speaking' response), the church's prayer for boldness quoting Psalm 2, and the believers' radical generosity introduced through Barnabas. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard, with names reintroduced periodically to avoid long unbroken runs of pronouns.

verses.text: Now a man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, also sold a piece of property.
His wife knew about it. Ananias kept back part of the money for himself, but he brought the rest and put it at the apostles' feet.
Then Peter said: Ananias, how is it that Satan has filled your heart to lie to the Holy Spirit and to keep for yourself some of the money you received for the land?
Did it not belong to you before it was sold? And after it was sold, was the money not yours to use? What made you think of doing such a thing? You have not lied just to human beings but to God.
When Ananias heard this, he fell down and died. And great fear came over all who heard what had happened.
Then some young men came forward, wrapped up his body, and carried him out and buried him.
About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter asked her: Tell me, is this the price you and Ananias got for the land? Yes, she said, that is the price.
Peter said to her: How could you and your husband agree together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Listen! The feet of the men who buried your husband are at the door, and they will carry you out also.
At that moment she fell down at his feet and died. Then the young men came in and, finding her dead, carried her out and buried her beside her husband.
Great fear came over the whole church and everyone who heard about these events.
The apostles did many signs and wonders among the people. All the believers used to meet together at Solomon's Porch.
No one else dared to join them, even though the people thought very highly of them.
Nevertheless, more and more men and women believed in the Lord and were added to their number.
Because of this, people brought the sick into the streets. They laid them on beds and mats, hoping that at least Peter's shadow might fall on some of them as he walked by.
Crowds also gathered from the towns around Jerusalem. They brought their sick people and those who were troubled by evil spirits, and all of them were healed.
Then the high priest and all his companions, who belonged to the group called the Sadducees, became very jealous.
They arrested the apostles and put them in the public jail.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the jail and brought them out. He said:
Go, stand in the temple courts and tell the people all about this new life.

At daybreak they went into the temple courts, just as they had been told, and began to teach the people. When the high priest and his companions arrived, they called together the council — the full group of the elders of Israel — and sent men to the jail to bring the apostles.
But on arriving at the jail, the officers did not find them there. So they went back and reported:
We found the jail securely locked, with the guards standing at the doors, but when we opened them, we found no one inside.
When they heard this report, the captain of the temple guard and the chief priests were confused. They wondered what this would lead to.
Then someone came and said: Look! The men you put in jail are standing in the temple courts teaching the people.
At that, the captain went with his officers and brought the apostles. They did not use force, because they feared that the people would stone them.
The apostles were brought in and made to stand before the council, to be questioned by the high priest.
He said: We gave you strict orders not to teach in this name. But you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you want to make us guilty of this man's blood.
Peter and the other apostles replied: We must obey God rather than human beings!
The God of our ancestors raised Jesus from the dead — whom you killed by hanging Him on a cross.
God lifted Jesus up to His own right hand, to be our Leader and Savior. God did this so that Israel could turn away from sin and be forgiven.
We are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him.
When they heard this, they were furious and wanted to put them to death.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honored by all the people, stood up in the council and ordered that the apostles be put outside for a little while.
Then he spoke to the council: My fellow Israelites, think carefully about what you plan to do to these men.
Some time ago Theudas appeared, claiming to be somebody important, and about four hundred men joined him. He was killed, all his followers were scattered, and it all came to nothing.
After him, Judas from Galilee appeared at the time when everyone had to be counted. He led a group of people to rebel. He too was killed, and all his followers were scattered.
So here is my advice for this case: Leave these men alone. Let them go. If what they are doing comes only from people, it will fail on its own.
But if it is from God, you will not be able to stop these men; you will only find yourselves fighting against God.
His speech persuaded them. They called the apostles in and had them flogged. Then they ordered them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
The apostles left the council full of joy, because they had been considered worthy to suffer shame for the name of Jesus.
Day after day, in the temple courts and from house to house, they never stopped teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Messiah.

5.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Ananias and Sapphira's judgment for lying to the Holy Spirit, the apostles' widespread healing ministry, their miraculous release from prison by an angel, and Gamaliel's cautionary counsel before the Sanhedrin. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: In those days, more and more people were becoming disciples. The Jews among them who spoke Greek began to complain against the Jews who spoke Hebrew, because the Greek-speaking widows were not getting their fair share of food each day.
So the twelve apostles gathered all the disciples together and said: It would not be right for us to stop teaching God's word so that we can serve food instead.
Brothers and sisters, choose seven men from among you who are known to be full of the Spirit and wisdom. We will turn this responsibility over to them,
And will give our attention to prayer and the ministry of the word.

This proposal pleased the whole group. They chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, along with Philip, Procorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas from Antioch, a convert to Judaism.
They presented these men to the apostles, who prayed and laid their hands on them.
So the word of God spread. The number of disciples in Jerusalem increased rapidly, and a large number of priests became obedient to the faith.
Now Stephen, a man full of God's grace and power, performed great wonders and signs among the people.

But some people stood against Stephen. They were from a synagogue called the Synagogue of the Freed Slaves. These Jews came from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia, and they began to argue with Stephen.
But they could not stand up against the wisdom the Spirit gave him as he spoke.
Then they secretly paid some men to say: We have heard Stephen say evil, insulting words against Moses and against God.
So they stirred up the people, the elders, and the teachers of the law. They grabbed Stephen and brought him before the council.
They brought in false witnesses who said: This man never stops speaking against this holy place and against the law.
For we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs that Moses gave to us.
All who were sitting in the council looked closely at Stephen, and they saw that his face looked like the face of an angel.

6.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the choosing of the seven (including Stephen) to serve the Hellenistic widows, and Stephen's arrest on false charges of blasphemy before the Sanhedrin.

verses.text: Then the high priest asked Stephen: Are these charges true?
Stephen replied: Brothers and fathers, listen to me! The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was still in Mesopotamia, before he lived in Harran.
God said to him: Leave your country and your people, and go to the land I will show you.
So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Harran. After the death of his father, God sent him to this land where you are now living.
God did not give Abraham any land there, not even enough ground to stand on. But God promised that Abraham and his family after him would own the land one day, even though Abraham had no child yet.
God spoke to him this way: Your family will be strangers living in a country that is not their own. The people there will make them slaves and treat them badly for four hundred years.
God said: But I will punish the nation that makes them slaves. After that, my people will come out of that country and worship me in this place.

Then God gave Abraham the sign of circumcision as a promise between them. So when Isaac was born, Abraham circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob became the father of the twelve family leaders of Israel.
Because the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph, they sold him as a slave into Egypt. But God was with him
God rescued Joseph from all his troubles. God gave Joseph wisdom and helped Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, like him. So Pharaoh made Joseph ruler over Egypt and over Pharaoh's whole palace.
Then a famine struck all Egypt and Canaan, bringing great suffering, and our ancestors could not find food.
When Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent our forefathers on their first visit.
On their second visit, Joseph told his brothers who he was, and Pharaoh learned about Joseph's family.
After this, Joseph sent for his father Jacob and his whole family, seventy-five in all.
Then Jacob went down to Egypt, where he and our ancestors died.
Their bodies were brought back to Shechem. They were placed in the tomb that Abraham had bought there from the sons of Hamor, paying a certain amount of money for it.
As the time got closer for God to keep His promise to Abraham, the number of our people in Egypt grew much larger.
Then a new king, to whom Joseph meant nothing, came to power in Egypt.
This king tricked and lied to our people. He treated our ancestors badly, forcing them to throw out their newborn babies so that the babies would die.
At that time Moses was born, and he was no ordinary child. For three months he was cared for by his family.
When he was placed outside, Pharaoh's daughter took him and brought him up as her own son.
Moses was educated in all the wisdom of the Egyptians and was powerful in speech and action.
When Moses was forty years old, he decided to visit his own people, the Israelites.
He saw an Egyptian treating one of them badly, so Moses stepped in to help him. Moses killed the Egyptian to get back at him for it.
Moses thought that his own people would realize that God was using him to rescue them, but they did not.
The next day Moses came upon two Israelites who were fighting. He tried to make peace between them by saying: Men, you are brothers. Why do you want to hurt each other?
But the man who was mistreating the other pushed Moses aside and said: Who made you ruler and judge over us?
Are you thinking of killing me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?
When Moses heard this, he fled to Midian, where he settled as a foreigner and had two sons.
After forty years had passed, an angel appeared to Moses in the flames of a burning bush in the desert near Mount Sinai.
When he saw this, he was amazed at the sight. As he went over to get a closer look, he heard the Lord say:
I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses trembled with fear and did not dare to look.
Then the Lord said to him: Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have indeed seen the oppression of my people in Egypt. I have heard their groaning and have come down to set them free. Now come, I will send you back to Egypt.

This is the same Moses that the people had rejected when they said: Who made you ruler and judge? But God sent Moses to be their ruler and to save them, with the help of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He led them out of Egypt and performed wonders and signs in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and for forty years in the wilderness.
This is the Moses who told the Israelites: God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people.
Moses was there with the people gathered in the wilderness. He was with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our ancestors. Moses received living words from God to pass on to us.
But our ancestors refused to obey him. Instead, they rejected him and in their hearts turned back to Egypt.
They told Aaron: Make us gods who will go before us. As for this Moses who led us out of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.
That was the time they made an idol shaped like a calf. They brought sacrifices to it, and they celebrated the thing that their own hands had made.

But God turned away from them and let them worship the sun, the moon, and the stars instead. This matches what is written in the book of the prophets: Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings for forty years in the wilderness, people of Israel?
You have carried the shrine of the god Molek and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made to worship. So I will send you away, far beyond Babylon.
Our ancestors had the sacred tent that held God's covenant with them in the wilderness. It was built just as God told Moses to build it, following the plan that Moses had seen.

After they received this tent, our ancestors, led by Joshua, brought it into the land. This was the land God took from the other nations and gave to our ancestors. The tent stayed in that land until the time of David,
David pleased God, and he asked if he could build a house for the God of Jacob to live in.
But it was Solomon who built the house for Him.
However, the Most High does not live in houses made by human hands. As the prophet says:
Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build for me? says the Lord. Or where will my resting place be?
Has not my hand made all these things?
You stubborn people! Your hearts and ears are still closed to God. You are just like your ancestors: you always fight against the Holy Spirit!
Was there ever a prophet that your ancestors did not hurt and chase away? They even killed the ones who said the Righteous One was coming. And now you have betrayed Him and killed Him —
You who received the law that was given through angels but have not obeyed it.
When the members of the council heard this, they were furious and ground their teeth at him in anger.
But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked up to heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
He said: Look! I see heaven open, and I see the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.
At this they covered their ears and, yelling at the top of their voices, they all rushed at him,
Dragged him out of the city and began to stone him. Meanwhile, the witnesses laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul.
While they were stoning him, Stephen prayed: Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
Then he fell on his knees and cried out: Lord, do not hold this sin against them. When he had said this, he fell asleep.

7.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Stephen's defense speech tracing Israel's history from Abraham through Joseph, Moses, and the tabernacle to the temple, his rebuke of the Sanhedrin, and his martyrdom by stoning -- including the first mention of Saul, who will become Paul. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: Saul agreed that Stephen should be killed. That same day, a time of great trouble and attacks began against the church in Jerusalem. All the believers except the apostles were scattered throughout Judea and Samaria.
Faithful men buried Stephen and cried deeply for him.
But Saul began to destroy the church. Going from house to house, he dragged off both men and women and put them in prison.
Those who had been scattered preached the word wherever they went.
Philip went down to a city in Samaria and told the people there about the Messiah.
When the crowds heard Philip and saw the signs he performed, they all paid close attention to what he said.
Evil spirits came out of many people, screaming loudly as they left. Many people who could not move or could not walk were healed.
So there was great joy in that city.
Now for some time, a man named Simon had used magic tricks in the city, and he amazed all the people of Samaria. He bragged that he was someone great,
All the people, important and ordinary, paid attention to him and said: This man is rightly called the Great Power of God.
They followed him because he had amazed them for a long time with his magic tricks.
But when they believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news of the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
Simon himself believed and was baptized. He followed Philip everywhere and was amazed by the great signs and miracles he saw.
When the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
When they arrived, they prayed for the new believers there that they might receive the Holy Spirit,
Because the Holy Spirit had not yet come on any of them. They had simply been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then Peter and John placed their hands on them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
When Simon saw that the Spirit was given at the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money
And said: Give me also this ability so that everyone on whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit.
Peter answered: May your money perish with you, because you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!
You have no part or share in this work, because your heart is not right before God.
Turn away from this evil, and pray to the Lord. Maybe He will forgive you for having such a thought in your heart.
For I see that you are full of bitterness, and sin has trapped you.
Then Simon answered: Pray to the Lord for me, so that nothing you have said may happen to me.
After Peter and John had preached the word of the Lord and told people about Jesus, they went back to Jerusalem. Along the way they preached the good news in many villages of Samaria.
Now an angel of the Lord said to Philip: Go south to the road, the desert road, that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza.
So Philip started out, and on his way he met an important Ethiopian official. This man was in charge of all the money for Candace, the queen of the Ethiopians. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship,
And on his way home was sitting in his chariot reading the Book of Isaiah the prophet.
The Spirit told Philip: Go to that chariot and stay near it.
Then Philip ran up to the chariot and heard the man reading from the prophet Isaiah. Philip asked: Do you understand what you are reading?
He said: How can I understand, unless someone explains it to me? Then he invited Philip to come up and sit with him.
This is the part of Scripture the official was reading: He was led like a sheep to be killed, and as a lamb stays silent while its wool is being cut off, so He did not open His mouth.
He was shamed, and justice was taken away from Him. Who can tell about the people who come after Him? Because His life was taken from the earth.
The official asked Philip: Tell me, please, who is the prophet talking about? Is it himself, or someone else?
Then Philip began with that very passage of Scripture and told him the good news about Jesus.
As they traveled along the road, they came to some water, and the official said: Look, here is water. What can stop me from being baptized?
Philip said: If you believe with all your heart, you may. And he answered: I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.
And he gave orders to stop the chariot. Then both Philip and the official went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.
When they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord suddenly took Philip away, and the official did not see him again. But the official went on his way full of joy.
Philip, however, appeared at Azotus and traveled about, preaching the gospel in all the towns until he reached Caesarea.

8.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the persecution and scattering of the Jerusalem church, Philip's ministry in Samaria including the confrontation with Simon the sorcerer, and Philip's encounter with the Ethiopian eunuch on the Gaza road. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still full of anger and threats to kill the Lord's disciples. He went to the high priest
He asked the high priest for letters to the synagogues in Damascus. He wanted permission that if he found any men or women there who followed the Way, he could take them as prisoners to Jerusalem.
As he neared Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him: Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me?
Saul asked: Who are You, Lord? He replied: I am Jesus, the One you are persecuting.
Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.
The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the sound but did not see anyone.
Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could see nothing. So his companions led him by the hand into Damascus.
For three days he was blind, and did not eat or drink anything.
In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord called to him in a vision: Ananias! He answered: Yes, Lord.
The Lord told him: Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.
In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.
Ananias answered: Lord, I have heard many reports about this man, and all the harm he has done to Your holy people in Jerusalem.
And he has come here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.
But the Lord said to Ananias: Go! This man is my chosen instrument to proclaim my name to the Gentiles and their kings and to the people of Israel.
I will show him how much he must suffer for my name.

Then Ananias went to the house and entered it. He placed his hands on Saul and said: Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me. He sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.
Immediately something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he could see again. He got up and was baptized,
And after taking some food, he regained his strength. Saul spent several days with the disciples in Damascus.
At once he began to preach in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

All those who heard him were amazed and asked: Is this not the man who caused so much trouble in Jerusalem for those who called on this name? And did he not come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?
Yet Saul grew more and more powerful, and he confused the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Messiah.
After many days had gone by, the Jews made a secret plan to kill him,
But Saul learned of their plan. Day and night they kept close watch on the city gates in order to kill him.
But his followers took him by night and lowered him in a basket through an opening in the wall.
When he came to Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he really was a disciple.

But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles. He told them how Saul had seen the Lord on his journey, and that the Lord had spoken to him. He also told them how in Damascus, Saul had preached fearlessly in the name of Jesus.
So Saul stayed with them and moved about freely in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.
He talked and argued with the Greek-speaking Jews, but they tried to kill him.
When the believers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had a time of peace and grew stronger. The believers lived with respect for the Lord, and the Holy Spirit encouraged them. More and more people joined them.
As Peter traveled about the country, he went to visit the Lord's people who lived in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas, who could not move and had been lying in bed for eight years.
Peter said to him: Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and roll up your mat. Right away, Aeneas got up.
All those who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha, whose name in Greek is Dorcas. She was always doing good and helping the poor.
About that time she became sick and died. Her body was washed and placed in an upstairs room.
Lydda was near Joppa, and the disciples, hearing that Peter was in Lydda, sent two men who urged him: Please come at once!

Peter went with them, and when he arrived, he was taken upstairs to the room. All the widows stood around him, crying. They showed him the robes and other clothes that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.
Peter sent them all out of the room. Then he got down on his knees and prayed. Turning toward the dead woman, he said: Tabitha, get up. She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.
He took her by the hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called for the believers, especially the widows, and presented her to them alive.
This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.
Peter stayed in Joppa for some time with a man named Simon, who made leather for a living.

9.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Saul's dramatic conversion on the road to Damascus, his blindness and healing through Ananias, his escape from Damascus and cautious reception by the apostles in Jerusalem through Barnabas's advocacy, and Peter's healings of Aeneas and Tabitha (Dorcas). All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: At Caesarea there was a man named Cornelius. He was an army officer in what was called the Italian Group of soldiers.
He and his whole family were faithful and respected God. He gave generously to those in need, and he prayed to God regularly.
One day at about three in the afternoon he had a vision. He distinctly saw an angel of God, who came to him and said: Cornelius!
Cornelius stared at him in fear and asked: What is it, Lord? The angel answered: Your prayers and your gifts to the poor have gone up to God like an offering He remembers.
Now send men to Joppa to bring back a man named Simon who is called Peter.
He is staying with Simon, a man who makes leather for a living, whose house is by the sea.
When the angel who spoke to him had gone, Cornelius called two of his servants and a faithful soldier, one of his personal helpers.
He told them everything that had happened and sent them to Joppa.
About noon the following day, as they were on their journey and approaching the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray.
He became hungry and wanted something to eat. While the meal was being prepared, Peter fell into a deep vision.
He saw heaven opened and something like a large sheet being let down to earth by its four corners.
It contained all kinds of four-footed animals, as well as reptiles and birds.
Then a voice told him: Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.
Peter replied: Surely not, Lord! I have never eaten anything unclean or forbidden.
The voice spoke to him a second time: Do not call anything unclean that God has made clean.
This happened three times, and immediately the sheet was taken back to heaven.
While Peter was wondering about the meaning of the vision, the men sent by Cornelius found out where Simon's house was and stopped at the gate.
They called out, asking if Simon who was known as Peter was staying there.
While Peter was still thinking about the vision, the Spirit said to him: Simon, three men are looking for you.
So get up and go downstairs. Do not be afraid to go with them, because I have sent them.
Peter went down and said to the men: I am the one you are looking for. Why have you come?

The men replied: We have come from Cornelius, an army officer. He is a good man who respects God, and all the Jewish people think highly of him. A holy angel told him to bring you to his house, so that he could hear what you have to say.
Then Peter invited the men into the house to be his guests. The next day Peter started out with them, and some of the believers from Joppa went along.
The following day he arrived in Caesarea. Cornelius was expecting them and had called together his relatives and close friends.
As Peter entered the house, Cornelius met him and bowed down at his feet to honor him.
But Peter made him get up. He said: Stand up. I am only a man myself.
While talking with him, Peter went inside and found a large gathering of people.

He said to them: You know well that it is against our law for a Jewish man to spend time with or visit someone who is not Jewish. But God has shown me that I should not call anyone unclean or unworthy.
So when you sent for me, I came without arguing. May I ask why you sent for me?
Cornelius answered: Four days ago I was in my house praying at this hour, at three in the afternoon. Suddenly a man in shining clothes stood before me
And said: Cornelius, God has heard your prayer and remembered your gifts to the poor.
Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter. He is a guest in the home of Simon, who makes leather for a living, and lives by the sea.
So I sent for you immediately, and it was good of you to come. Now we are all here in the presence of God to listen to everything the Lord has commanded you to tell us.
Then Peter began to speak: I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism
But accepts from every nation the one who fears Him and does what is right.
You know the message God sent to the people of Israel, announcing the good news of peace through Jesus Christ, who is Lord of all.
You know what has happened throughout the province of Judea, beginning in Galilee after the baptism that John preached —
How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power, and how He went around doing good and healing all who were under the power of the devil, because God was with Him.
We are witnesses of everything He did in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed Him by hanging Him on a cross,
But God raised Him from the dead on the third day and let people see Him.
He was not seen by all the people, but by witnesses whom God had already chosen — by us who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
He commanded us to preach to the people and to tell them that He is the one whom God appointed as judge of the living and the dead.
All the prophets speak about Him, saying that everyone who believes in Him receives forgiveness of sins through His name.
While Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit came on all who heard the message.
The Jewish believers who had come with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out even on the non-Jewish people.
For they heard them speaking in other languages and praising God. Then Peter said:
Surely no one can stand in the way of their being baptized with water. They have received the Holy Spirit just as we have.
So he ordered that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked Peter to stay with them for a few days.

10.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Cornelius's vision of an angel, Peter's vision of the sheet with unclean animals, Peter's sermon at Cornelius's household, and the Holy Spirit falling on Gentile believers for the first time -- the pivotal moment where the gospel is confirmed to be for all nations, not Jews only. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: The apostles and the believers all through Judea heard that the non-Jewish people had also received the word of God.
When Peter went up to Jerusalem, the Jewish believers criticized him.
They said: You went into the house of non-Jewish men and ate with them.
Peter began to explain everything to them, just as it had happened:

I was in the city of Joppa praying. I fell into a trance and saw a vision. I saw something like a large sheet coming down from heaven. It was let down by its four corners, and it came down to where I was.
I looked closely and saw animals with four feet, wild animals, reptiles, and birds.
Then I heard a voice telling me: Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.
I replied: Never, Lord! I have never eaten anything unclean.
The voice spoke from heaven again: Do not call anything unclean that God has made clean.
This happened three times, and then it was all pulled up to heaven again.
Just then, three men sent to me from Caesarea arrived at the house where I was staying.
The Spirit told me not to hesitate to go with them. These six brothers went with me too, and we all went into the man's house.
He told us that he had seen an angel standing in his house. The angel said: Send men to Joppa for Simon, who is called Peter.
He will bring you a message. Through it, you and everyone in your house will be saved.
As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came on them as He had come on us at the beginning.
Then I remembered what the Lord had said: John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
God gave them the same gift He gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ. So who was I to think I could stand in God's way?
When they heard this, they stopped objecting and praised God. They said: So then, God has given the non-Jewish people the chance to turn away from sin and live.
Now the believers who had been scattered because of the persecution that started when Stephen was killed had traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch. They spread the word only among Jews.
But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch. They began to speak to Greeks too, telling them the good news about the Lord Jesus.
The Lord's power was with them, and many people believed and turned to the Lord.
News of this reached the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
When Barnabas arrived and saw what the grace of God had done, he was glad. He encouraged everyone to stay true to the Lord with all their hearts.
Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith. Many more people were brought to the Lord.
Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul,
When he found Saul, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year, Barnabas and Saul met with the church and taught many people. The disciples were called Christians first at Antioch.
During this time some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, named Agabus, stood up. Through the Spirit, he predicted that a bad famine would spread over the whole Roman world. This happened while Claudius was emperor.
So the disciples decided that each one would give what he could to help the brothers and sisters living in Judea.
They did this, and sent their gift to the elders through Barnabas and Saul.

11.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Peter's defense of his visit to Cornelius before the circumcised believers in Jerusalem, the founding of the multi-ethnic church at Antioch (where believers were first called Christians), Barnabas bringing Saul to help lead it, and the prophecy of Agabus prompting famine relief for Judea. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: About this time, King Herod arrested some people who belonged to the church. He wanted to hurt them.
He had James, the brother of John, killed with a sword.
When Herod saw that this pleased the Jewish leaders, he also arrested Peter. This happened during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
After arresting Peter, Herod put him in prison. He handed Peter over to four groups of four soldiers to guard him. Herod planned to bring him out for public trial after the Passover.
So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was praying hard to God for him.
The night before Herod planned to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers. He was bound with two chains, and guards stood watch at the entrance.
Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared, and a light shone in the cell. The angel hit Peter on the side to wake him up. He said: Quick, get up! Then the chains fell off Peter's wrists.
Then the angel said to him: Put on your clothes and sandals. Peter did this. The angel said: Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.
Peter followed him out of the prison. But he did not know that what the angel was doing was really happening. He thought he was seeing a vision.

They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate that led to the city. It opened for them by itself, and they walked through it. When they had walked the length of one street, the angel suddenly left him.
Then Peter came to his senses and said: Now I know for certain that the Lord sent His angel. He rescued me from Herod's power and from everything the Jewish people were hoping would happen to me.
When Peter realized this, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John (also called Mark). Many people had gathered there and were praying.
Peter knocked at the outer entrance, and a servant named Rhoda came to answer the door.
When Rhoda recognized Peter's voice, she was so happy that she ran back without opening the door. She said: Peter is at the door!
They said to her: You are out of your mind. But she kept insisting it was true. So they said: It must be his angel.
But Peter kept on knocking. When they opened the door and saw him, they were amazed.
Peter motioned with his hand for them to be quiet. He told them how the Lord had brought him out of prison. He said: Tell James and the other believers about this. Then he left for another place.
In the morning, the soldiers were very upset, wondering what had happened to Peter.
Herod searched everywhere for Peter but could not find him. So he questioned the guards and ordered them to be put to death. Then Herod went from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.

Herod had been angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon. So they joined together and asked to meet with him. First they won the support of Blastus, a trusted servant of the king. Then they asked for peace, because they depended on the king's country for their food.
On the chosen day, Herod put on his royal robes, sat on his throne, and gave a speech to the people.
They shouted: This is the voice of a god, not of a man.
Right away, an angel of the Lord struck Herod down, because he did not give the praise to God. Herod was eaten by worms and died.
But the word of God continued to spread and grow.

12.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers King Herod's persecution of the church including James's martyrdom, Peter's angel-assisted escape from prison, the church's prayer meeting at Mary's house (including Rhoda's excited response at the door), and Herod's sudden death for accepting worship as a god. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard; angels are not capitalized, matching the convention used throughout this site.

verses.text: In the church at Antioch, there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon (called Niger), Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen (who had grown up with Herod the ruler), and Saul.
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: Set apart Barnabas and Saul for me. I have called them to do special work.
So after they had fasted and prayed, they placed their hands on them and sent them off.
The Holy Spirit sent Barnabas and Saul on their way. They went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
When they arrived at Salamis, they preached the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. John was with them as their helper.
They traveled through the whole island until they came to Paphos. There they met a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus,
Bar-Jesus was a close helper of the governor, Sergius Paulus. The governor was a smart man. He sent for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God.
But Elymas the sorcerer (that is what his name means) fought against them. He tried to turn the governor away from the faith.
Then Saul, who was also called Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit. He looked straight at Elymas
And said: You are a child of the devil! You are an enemy of everything that is right. You are full of lies and tricks. Will you never stop twisting the right ways of the Lord?

Now the hand of the Lord is against you. You will be blind for a while. You will not even be able to see the light of the sun. Right away, mist and darkness came over Elymas. He walked around trying to find someone to lead him by the hand.
When the governor saw what had happened, he believed. He was amazed at the teaching about the Lord.
From Paphos, Paul and his companions sailed to Perga in Pamphylia. There, John left them and went back to Jerusalem.
From Perga they went on to Pisidian Antioch. On the Sabbath they entered the synagogue and sat down.
After the reading from the Law and the Prophets, the synagogue leaders sent word to them. They said: Brothers, if you have a word of encouragement for the people, please speak.
Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said: Fellow Israelites, and you non-Jewish people who worship God, listen to me!
The God of the people of Israel chose our ancestors. He made them do well while they were foreigners in Egypt. Then, with great power, He led them out of that country,
And for about forty years He put up with them in the wilderness.
He defeated seven nations in Canaan and gave their land to His people to keep.
All this took about four hundred and fifty years. After this, God gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
Then the people asked for a king. God gave them Saul, son of Kish, from the tribe of Benjamin. Saul ruled for forty years.
After removing Saul, God made David their king. God said about David: I have found David, son of Jesse, a man after my own heart. He will do everything I want him to do.
From this man's descendants God has brought to Israel the Savior He promised — Jesus.
Before Jesus came, John preached that all the people of Israel should turn from sin and be baptized.
As John was finishing his work, he said: Who do you think I am? I am not the one you are looking for. But there is One coming after me. I am not good enough to untie His sandals.
Fellow children of Abraham, and you non-Jewish people who worship God, this message of salvation has been sent to us.
The people of Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize Jesus. But by condemning Him, they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
They found no real reason to put Jesus to death, but they still asked Pilate to have Him killed.
When they had carried out all that was written about Him, they took Him down from the cross and laid Him in a tomb.
But God raised Him from the dead,
For many days after that, He was seen by those who had traveled with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now His witnesses to our people.
We tell you the good news: What God promised our ancestors
God has fulfilled this promise for us, their children, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second Psalm: You are my Son. Today I have become your father.
God raised Jesus from the dead so that His body would never rot. As God has said: I will give you the holy and sure blessings promised to David.
So it is also said in another place: You will not let Your Holy One see decay.
When David had served God's purpose in his own lifetime, he died. He was buried with his ancestors, and his body decayed.
But the One whom God raised from the dead did not decay.
So, my friends, I want you to know this: through Jesus, the forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
Through Him, everyone who believes is set free from every sin. This is something the law of Moses could never do for you.
Take care that what the prophets have said does not happen to you:
Look, you who mock! Be amazed, and then die, for I am going to do something in your days that you would never believe, even if someone told you.
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the people invited them to speak further about these things on the next Sabbath.
When the meeting ended, many of the Jews and devout converts to Judaism followed Paul and Barnabas. Paul and Barnabas talked with them and urged them to continue trusting in the grace of God.
On the next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
When the Jews saw the crowds, they became jealous. They began to argue against what Paul was saying and insulted him.

Then Paul and Barnabas answered them boldly: We had to speak the word of God to you first. But you reject it. You do not consider yourselves worthy of eternal life. So now we turn to the non-Jewish people.
For this is what the Lord has commanded us: I have made you a light for the non-Jewish people, so that you may bring salvation to the ends of the earth.
When the non-Jewish people heard this, they were glad and honored the word of the Lord. All who were chosen for eternal life believed.
The word of the Lord spread through the whole region.
But the Jewish leaders stirred up the God-fearing women of high standing and the leading men of the city. They caused trouble for Paul and Barnabas and threw them out of their region.
So they shook the dust off their feet as a warning to them and went to Iconium.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.

13.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the Holy Spirit's commissioning of Barnabas and Saul at Antioch, the start of the first missionary journey through Cyprus (including the confrontation with Elymas the sorcerer and the first use of the name 'Paul'), and Paul's synagogue sermon at Pisidian Antioch tracing Israel's history to Jesus. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: At Iconium, Paul and Barnabas went as usual into the Jewish synagogue. They spoke so well that a great number of Jews and Greeks believed.
But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up the other non-Jewish people. They turned their minds against the brothers.
So Paul and Barnabas stayed there a long time, speaking boldly for the Lord. The Lord proved that His message of grace was true by letting them perform signs and wonders.
The people of the city were divided; some sided with the Jews, others with the apostles.
The non-Jewish people and Jews, together with their leaders, made a plan to hurt Paul and Barnabas and stone them.
But they found out about it and fled to the Lycaonian cities of Lystra and Derbe and to the surrounding country,
Where they kept on preaching the good news.
In Lystra there sat a man who was lame. He had been that way from birth and had never walked.
He listened to Paul speaking. Paul looked directly at him, saw that he had faith to be healed,
And called out: Stand up on your feet! At that, the man jumped up and began to walk.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they shouted in the Lycaonian language: The gods have come down to us, looking like humans!
They called Barnabas Zeus, and they called Paul Hermes, because he did most of the talking.
The priest of Zeus had a temple just outside the city. He brought bulls and flowers to the city gates because he and the crowd wanted to offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas.
But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of this, they tore their clothes and rushed out into the crowd, shouting:

Friends, why are you doing this? We are only human too, just like you. We are bringing you good news. We are telling you to turn away from these worthless things and turn to the living God, who made heaven, earth, the sea, and everything in them.
In the past, He let all nations go their own way.
But He has always shown you proof that He is real. He has shown kindness by giving you rain from heaven and crops at the right time. He gives you plenty of food and fills your hearts with joy.
Even after saying all this, Paul and Barnabas could barely stop the crowd from sacrificing to them.
Then some Jews came from Antioch and Iconium and won the crowd over. They stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking he was dead.
But after the disciples had gathered around him, Paul got up and went back into the city. The next day, he and Barnabas left for Derbe.
They preached the good news in Derbe and gained many disciples. Then they went back to Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch,
They strengthened the disciples and encouraged them to remain true to the faith. They said: We must go through many hard times to enter the kingdom of God.
Paul and Barnabas appointed elders for them in each church. With prayer and fasting, they gave these elders over to the Lord, in whom they had put their trust.
After going through Pisidia, they came into Pamphylia,
And when they had preached the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
From Attalia, they sailed back to Antioch. This was the place where they had been given over to the grace of God for the work they had now finished.
When they arrived, they gathered the church together. They reported all that God had done through them, and how He had opened the door of faith to the non-Jewish people.
And they stayed there a long time with the disciples.

14.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers Paul and Barnabas's ministry at Iconium and Lystra, including healing a man lame from birth, being mistaken for the gods Zeus and Hermes, Paul's stoning and miraculous recovery, and the return journey appointing elders and strengthening the young churches. All pronouns referring to God are capitalized per this site's standard; the Greek/Roman gods Zeus and Hermes are not capitalized as pronouns since they are not the God of this site's convention.

verses.text: Some men came down from Judea to Antioch. They taught the believers: Unless you are circumcised the way Moses taught, you cannot be saved.

This caused a sharp argument between Paul and Barnabas and these men. So the church chose Paul and Barnabas, along with some other believers, to go up to Jerusalem. They were to talk with the apostles and elders about this question.
The church sent them on their way. As they traveled through Phoenicia and Samaria, they told how the non-Jewish people had turned to God. This news made all the believers very glad.
When they came to Jerusalem, the church, the apostles, and the elders welcomed them. Paul and Barnabas reported everything God had done through them.
Then some believers who belonged to the group called the Pharisees stood up and said: The non-Jewish people must be circumcised. They must be required to keep the law of Moses.
The apostles and elders met to consider this question.
After much discussion, Peter stood up and spoke to them: Brothers, you know that some time ago God chose me from among you. Through me, the non-Jewish people heard the good news and believed.
God knows every heart. He showed that He accepted them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as He did for us.
He made no difference between us and them. He made their hearts clean through faith.
So now, why do you try to test God? Why put a heavy burden on the non-Jewish disciples that neither we nor our ancestors could carry?
No! We believe it is through the grace of our Lord Jesus that we are saved, just as they are.
The whole group became silent as they listened to Barnabas and Paul. Barnabas and Paul told about the signs and wonders God had done among the non-Jewish people through them.
When they finished, James spoke up: Brothers, listen to me.
Simon has told us how God first acted to choose a people for His name from the non-Jewish people.
The words of the prophets are in agreement with this, as it is written:
After this I will return and rebuild David's fallen tent. Its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
So that the rest of humanity may seek the Lord, even all the non-Jewish people who bear my name, says the Lord, who does these things
That have been known for ages.
So it is my judgment that we should not make it hard for the non-Jewish people who are turning to God.
Instead, we should write to them. We should tell them to stay away from food offered to idols, from sexual sin, from the meat of animals that were strangled, and from blood.
For the law of Moses has been preached in every city from the earliest times and is read in the synagogues on every Sabbath.

Then the apostles and elders, with the whole church, decided to choose some of their own men and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They chose Judas, called Barsabbas, and Silas, two leaders among the believers.
With them they sent this letter: From the apostles and elders, your brothers. To the non-Jewish believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
We have heard that some men went out from us without our permission. They troubled you and confused your minds by what they said.
So we all agreed to choose some men and send them to you with our dear friends Barnabas and Paul,
Men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we are sending Judas and Silas. They will tell you in person the same things we are writing.
It seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us not to burden you with anything beyond the following requirements:
You are to abstain from food sacrificed to idols, from blood, from the meat of strangled animals, and from sexual immorality. You will do well to avoid these things. Farewell.
So the men were sent off and went down to Antioch, where they gathered the church together and delivered the letter.
The people read it and were glad for its encouraging message.
Judas and Silas, who themselves were prophets, said much to encourage and strengthen the believers.
After spending some time there, they were sent off by the believers with the blessing of peace to return to those who had sent them.
But Silas decided to remain there.
But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, where they and many others taught and preached the word of the Lord.
Some time later Paul said to Barnabas: Let us go back and visit the believers in all the towns where we preached the word of the Lord and see how they are doing.
Barnabas wanted to take John, also called Mark, with them,
But Paul did not think it wise to take him, because he had deserted them in Pamphylia and had not continued with them in the work.
They had such a sharp disagreement that they parted company. Barnabas took Mark and sailed for Cyprus,
But Paul chose Silas and left, commended by the believers to the grace of the Lord.
He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.

15.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Greek text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. Covers the Jerusalem Council's pivotal decision that Gentile believers need not be circumcised or keep the full law of Moses, James's citation of the prophets, the letter sent to Antioch, and the sharp split between Paul and Barnabas over John Mark that led to two missionary teams instead of one. All pronouns referring to God, Jesus, and the Holy Spirit are capitalized per this site's standard.

verses.text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul took the road through the interior and arrived at Ephesus. There he found some disciples
And asked them: Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed? They answered: No, we have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.
So Paul asked: Then what baptism did you receive? John's baptism, they replied.
Paul said: John's baptism was a baptism of repentance. He told the people to believe in the one coming after him, that is, in Jesus.
On hearing this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied.
There were about twelve men in all.
Paul entered the synagogue and spoke boldly there for three months, arguing persuasively about the kingdom of God.
But some of them became obstinate and refused to believe, publicly maligning the Way. So Paul left them and took the disciples with him and had discussions daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
This went on for two years, so that all the Jews and Greeks who lived in the province of Asia heard the word of the Lord.
God did extraordinary miracles through Paul,
So that even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and their illnesses were cured and the evil spirits left them.

Some Jews who traveled around driving out evil spirits tried to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who were demon-possessed. They would say: In the name of the Jesus whom Paul preaches, I command you to come out.
Seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
One day the evil spirit answered them: Jesus I know, and Paul I know about, but who are you?
Then the man who had the evil spirit jumped on them and overpowered them all. He gave them such a beating that they ran out of the house naked and bleeding.
When this became known to the Jews and Greeks living in Ephesus, they were all seized with fear, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honor.
Many of those who believed now came and openly confessed what they had done.
A number who had practiced sorcery brought their scrolls together and burned them publicly. When they calculated the value of the scrolls, the total came to fifty thousand drachmas.
In this way the word of the Lord spread widely and grew in power.
After all this had happened, Paul decided to go to Jerusalem, passing through Macedonia and Achaia. I must visit Rome also, he said.
He sent two of his helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia, while he stayed in the province of Asia a little longer.
About that time there arose a great disturbance about the Way.
A silversmith named Demetrius, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought in a lot of business for the craftsmen there.
He called them together, along with the workers in related trades, and said: You know, my friends, that we receive a good income from this business.

And you see and hear how this fellow Paul has convinced and led astray large numbers of people here in Ephesus and in practically the whole province of Asia. He says that gods made by human hands are no gods at all.

There is danger not only that our trade will lose its good name, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be discredited, and the goddess herself, who is worshiped throughout the province of Asia and the world, will be robbed of her divine majesty.
When they heard this, they were furious and began shouting: Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!
